title: Stratified Regression Suite for KV Prefix Cache Behavioral Shifts
creator: Asha Natarajan
description: Build a statistically rigorous, stratified regression test harness that detects functional and semantic shifts caused by KV/prefix cache hits across config and model changes. The suite will evaluate per-token and per-response deltas, use significance testing to avoid noisy alerts, and integrate with Canary + Console gating so rollouts can be automatically held for suspicious regressions.
motivation: Recent deployments and config flips (kernel selection, batch windowing, cache prefetch heuristics) produced cryptic user-visible regressions tied to cache hits. Existing canaries surface high-level delta rates but lack stratification by prompt archetype, token-position, and model-variant. We need an automated suite that separates benign micro-differences (non-semantic token-level divergences) from high-risk semantic regressions and controls rollout decisions.
scope: Implement stratified prompt bucket generation (short Q/A, long-form context, code generation, instruction-following, edge-case tokens)
Token-aligned replay that reconstructs cache hit traces and replays requests with/without hit to isolate behavior
Statistical test pipeline (bootstrap, paired Wilcoxon, effect size) to flag meaningful deltas
Embedding-based semantic similarity and intent-preservation checks for hit vs. miss outputs
Integrate with Console canary charts and automated rollout gating via the existing rollout API
Run nightly baseline against release branches and maintain artifactized golden responses for regression triage
out_of_scope: Full replacement of existing end-to-end canary infra (we will integrate, not rewrite)
A/B testing UX in Console - analytics will be surfaced but UX changes are product work
Model-architecture-level kernel rewrites (research will own optimization patches)
success_metrics: False-positive rate < 5% for nightly alerts over a 30-day window (measured against manual triage)
Time-to-detect code/config regressions <= 1 hour after rollout when using automated probes
Reduction in customer-facing incidents attributable to cache-hit drift by 50% in three months
Coverage: at least 6 stratified prompt buckets and 3 model families for initial rollout
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline can run isolated replay for a given request ID and return hit/miss paired outputs
Automated statistical test run returns a human-readable delta summary and an Alert Decision (OK/HOLD/ESCALATE)
Canary UI dashboard shows stratified delta heatmaps (per-prompt-bucket, per-token-pos, per-model-variant)
Rollout API integration: a flagged regression toggles canary to HOLD and posts triage ticket with summary and links
Documented runbook and triage checklist in Drive + one example incident postmortem demonstrating workflow
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2w): Design stratification schema and dataset seed; implement token-aligned replay harness; add traffic-capture adapter
Phase 2 (2w): Build statistical test microservice and standardize delta report schema; create embedding-similarity checks
Phase 3 (1w): Console integration and canary gating wiring; dashboard prototypes with mock data
Phase 4 (1w): End-to-end smoke on staging, generate golden artifacts, run sweep across 3 model families
Phase 5 (ongoing): Nightly runs, alert tuning, add additional prompt buckets and adversarial prompts
data_and_eval_plan: Seed dataset composed of 18k prompts stratified across 6 buckets: short-QA, multi-turn chat, long-narrative, code-snippet, instruction-following, adversarial edge-cases
For each prompt execute: baseline miss (cache disabled), hit-enabled baseline, and N permutations for randomness control
Metrics collected per pair: token-level edit distance, normalized log-prob delta, embedding cosine similarity (512-d), and label-preserving classifier output
Statistical approach: paired bootstrap CI on response similarity, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank for non-parametric signal, and Cliff's delta for effect size
Thresholds: embedding cosine < 0.92 + effect size > 0.2 => semantic-regression candidate (tunable via alerts)
Store artifacts: canonical response pairs, spectrogram of token diffs, and minimal reproducible replay script in artifact bucket
monitoring_and_alerting: Create metric series: kv_hit_semantic_regressions.count, kv_hit_token_drift.rate, kv_hit_per_bucket.false_positive_adj
Set alert rules: P1 if regressions > 10 across any customer-impacting bucket in last 15m; P2 if > 50 across all buckets in 24h
Integrate with Slack #canary-alerts and create automated triage ticket with links to artifacts and suggested rollback config
Add trace hooks to runtime to emit hit-signature (opaque hash) to correlate request <-> replay artifacts
Retention: keep regression artifacts for 90 days and snapshots for last 5 releases
rollout_strategy: Start with internal canary: 0.5% traffic for 24h across dedicated test orgs
If no HOLD decision, expand to staged canary 5% for 6h then 25% for 24h
Automatic HOLD on semantic-regression candidate from tiered buckets; manual review required to proceed
For high-confidence regressions, auto-trigger rollback to previous runtime release and notify oncall
Post-rollout: run full-nightly sweep and publish regression summary to relevant squads
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-sensitive thresholds causing alert fatigue -> Mitigation: tune with 30-day historical playback and add silencing rules
Risk: Replay non-determinism due to upstream randomness -> Mitigation: seed RNGs, snapshot model-variant, and isolate external tool calls
Risk: Cost of nightly runs across many model variants -> Mitigation: priority bucketing and incremental expand-on-pass; sample-based runs for low-risk buckets
Risk: Telemetry privacy for customer prompts -> Mitigation: apply PII scrubbing and hash-only stored traces for customer data
